initial_observation.encounter_context: presented to Banner Desert Medical Center for evaluation of respiratory distress and weight loss
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: On physical exam, a significant murmur was heard that had not previously been noted on prior exams. Initial echocardiogram revealed a left pulmonary arterial sling, prominent patent foramen ovale, and a moderate size patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with continuous left to right shunting.

evidence_items.source_text: Initial echocardiogram revealed a left pulmonary arterial sling, prominent patent foramen ovale, and a moderate size patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with continuous left to right shunting.

Subsequent CT angiogram confirmed a pulmonary sling, with the left pulmonary artery arising from the distal right pulmonary artery and wrapping around the distal trachea (Fig. 2). Left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, consistent with left-sided air trapping, was observed. Moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and a notable patent foramen ovale (PFO) were present. Furthermore, a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus) was identified (Fig. 3).

At 7-months-old the patient underwent left pulmonary artery sling and PDA repair with re-implantation of the left pulmonary artery into the main pulmonary artery anterior to the trachea and PDA division/ligation. She developed postoperative left pulmonary artery stenosis and underwent successful balloon angioplasty. Unfortunately, due to the significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia she developed recurrent left pulmonary artery stenosis.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: left pulmonary arterial sling with an associated right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus)
accepted_aliases: pulmonary artery sling with tracheal bronchus
pulmonary artery sling with a pig bronchus
